Name: Whispers_01_ClockTenMinutes
line: Ten minutes, goblin. How goes the arson? …Don't answer. I can smell it from here.
note: §2.2 clock pressure: the Overlord's whispers check in at the 10-minute mark; tier-1 register is mockery, not mourning.

Name: Whispers_02_ClockFiveMinutes
line: Five minutes. My stones are back through the trees, goblin — follow the road out and keep the mill at your back. Start walking while you gloat.
note: §2.2: at 5 minutes the whisper names a direction; the direction rides only on §2.8's authored wayfinding cues (converging roads, the windmill silhouette over the treetops), and §2.1 places the runic site in the forest clearing beyond the trees.

Name: Whispers_03_ClockTwoMinutes
line: Two minutes. There. The circle. Into it. Drop the chicken if you must — …don't drop the chicken.
note: §2.2: inside the final 2 the Overlord points you at the extraction outright; portal dies at 0:00 plus a 90-second collapse. Chicken is a §2.9 loot-kind steal.

Name: Whispers_04_ObjectiveGranaryFirstTorch
line: Their whole winter, goblin, stacked in one shed — with every spear in the hamlet standing round it. Light it and let them argue about badgers.
note: Sibling of the windmill Stage-1 bark for the §2.8 granary: a compact blaze in the village core where the guards are thickest, plus the §2.10 denial joke. First-time dismissible prompt per §2.8.

Name: Whispers_05_ObjectiveFieldFirstTorch
line: One row takes the next, goblin. Set the edge alight and walk away — the wheat does my work while they queue at the well with buckets.
note: Sibling of the windmill Stage-1 bark for the §2.8 wheat field: fire spreads row to row, the most visible arson and the hardest to douse; §2.6 bucket brigade forms at the well.

Name: Whispers_06_MilestoneFirstLootBanked
line: The first sack crosses into my stones. It is mine now. No bell in Groatsworth can un-steal it.
note: §2.7/§2.6/§1: physical loot banks permanently the instant it reaches the stones, wipe-proof.

Name: Whispers_07_MilestoneFirstPigBanked
line: A pig. Through the ancient portal of His Eternal Darkness. …Set it down gently. It is banked, and it is beautiful.
note: §2.9 stolen pig is loot-kind (40) and banks on delivery; §2.10 apocalyptic gravitas applied to stealing pigs.

Name: Whispers_08_MilestoneFirstPrisonerBanked
line: One of them, roped and walking into the dark. He'll know the word 'goblin' by morning. This is the tribute I wanted.
note: §2.6/§2.7: bound civilians are loot that walks itself, banking at the stones; marching prisoners home is the tribute His Eternal Darkness actually wants, not a body count.

Name: Whispers_09_MilestoneNoneLeftBehind
line: Every villager in the hamlet, marched home alive. Let the empty routines explain themselves. Who do they blame now — the badger?
note: §2.9 'None Left Behind' +40 is scored as every civilian in the hamlet marched home alive (bind/capture applies to civilians only, §2.6); §2.10 the denial straining — one missing villager is a badger, a whole hamlet's worth is the punchline landing.

Name: Whispers_10_MilestonePortalOpen
line: Granary, field, mill — all three ash. The stones are open, goblin. Come home; nothing else in this county will keep you.
note: §2.1/§1: burning the last of the three objectives flares the stones open as the extraction portal; §2.8 this hamlet carries one of each.

Name: Whispers_11_EndExtractionCaptureHeavy
line: You brought me a rope of them, blinking and alive. Not coins — proof they remember us. …Adequate.
note: §2.10 asks explicitly for a distinct verdict flavor when the raid comes home with a rope chain of prisoners: 'Bring me proof they remember us. …adequate.'

Name: Whispers_12_EndExtractionRichOnly
line: Gold, gold, and a pig. Very shiny, goblin. I have seen rats haul more, and rats bring me witnesses. …Adequate.
note: §2.10's 'merely rich' counterpart to the capture verdict, keeping the §2.1 rats crack; tier 1 mocks more than it mourns.

Name: Whispers_13_EndWipeLivesSpent
line: Five deaths, goblin. Your deeds keep a quarter of themselves; the rest burned where you fell. What reached my stones is still mine. Mostly mine.
note: §2.2/§1 loss condition: all 5 lives spent, only 25% of unbanked deeds kept, while loot already at the stones or the Warren is safe.

Name: Whispers_14_EndLeftBehind
line: The stones have gone cold and you are still out there, holding a chicken. Keep it. Groatsworth is your home now. …I'll tell them it was a badger.
note: §2.2/§1 loss condition: outside the circle when the portal dies after the 90-second collapse, whispers going cold; §2.10 badger denial joke.
